name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
description: Extend one arm in front with your palm up and gently pull your fingers back with the other hand for 20 seconds. It eases tightness in the forearm and wrist from typing or gripping. No equipment is needed.

name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
description: Extend one arm with your palm down and gently pull your fingers toward the floor for 20 seconds. It improves forearm strength and grip for daily tasks. No equipment is needed.

name: Wrist Curl
description: Rest your forearm on your thigh and curl a light dumbbell upward by bending only your wrist. It eases tightness in the forearm and wrist from typing or gripping. It requires a light dumbbell.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm down and lift a light dumbbell by bending only your wrist. It improves forearm strength and grip for daily tasks. It requires a light dumbbell.

name: Grip Squeeze
description: Squeeze a soft ball in your hand for five seconds, then release. It eases tightness in the forearm and wrist from typing or gripping. It requires a soft ball.

name: Finger Spread
description: Open your hand wide, spreading your fingers as far apart as is comfortable, then close into a loose fist. It improves forearm strength and grip for daily tasks. No equipment is needed.

name: Forearm Rotation
description: Hold a light weight with your elbow at your side and rotate your forearm palm up and palm down. It eases tightness in the forearm and wrist from typing or gripping. It requires a light weight.

name: Triceps Band Extension
description: Anchor a resistance band overhead and press your hands down by straightening your elbows. It improves forearm strength and grip for daily tasks. It requires a resistance band.

name: Elbow Flexion Stretch
description: Rest your arm on a table and gently bend and straighten your elbow through its comfortable range. It eases tightness in the forearm and wrist from typing or gripping. It requires a table.

name: Tennis Elbow Eccentric Extension
description: Lift a light weight with your wrist bent up using the other hand, then lower it slowly with the sore arm. It improves forearm strength and grip for daily tasks. It requires a light weight.

name: Towel Scrunch
description: Sit with your foot on a small towel and scrunch it toward you using only your toes. It supports foot control and ankle strength for standing and walking. It requires a small towel.

name: Marble Pickup
description: Pick up marbles with your toes and drop them into a cup. It builds the small muscles of the foot that help with balance. It requires marbles and a cup.

name: Ankle Alphabet
description: Trace each letter of the alphabet in the air with your big toe. It supports foot control and ankle strength for standing and walking. No equipment is needed.

name: Band Dorsiflexion
description: Anchor a resistance band and pull your toes up toward your shin against the resistance. It builds the small muscles of the foot that help with balance. It requires a resistance band.

name: Band Eversion
description: Loop a resistance band around your foot and turn the sole outward against the resistance. It supports foot control and ankle strength for standing and walking. It requires a resistance band.

name: Toe Raise
description: Stand with your heels on the floor and lift your toes as high as you can, then lower them. It builds the small muscles of the foot that help with balance. No equipment is needed.

name: Foot Roll on Ball
description: Roll the sole of your foot slowly over a tennis ball for one to two minutes. It supports foot control and ankle strength for standing and walking. It requires a tennis ball.

name: Short Foot Exercise
description: Sit with your foot flat and draw the ball of the foot toward your heel without curling your toes. It builds the small muscles of the foot that help with balance. No equipment is needed.

name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
description: Tilt your head to one side and gently pull it with your hand for 20 seconds. It relieves tension from desk work and improves posture. No equipment is needed.

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
description: Turn your head 45 degrees and tuck your chin toward your armpit, adding gentle hand pressure. It loosens the upper back and neck after long periods of sitting. No equipment is needed.

name: Neck Rotation
description: Slowly turn your head to look over each shoulder, holding for five seconds. It relieves tension from desk work and improves posture. No equipment is needed.

name: Thoracic Extension over Chair
description: Sit with your hands behind your head and arch your upper back gently over the chair back. It loosens the upper back and neck after long periods of sitting. It requires a sturdy chair.

name: Thread the Needle
description: From hands and knees, slide one arm under your body and rotate your upper back. It relieves tension from desk work and improves posture. No equipment is needed.

name: Wall Angel
description: Stand with your back against a wall and slide your arms up and down like a snow angel. It loosens the upper back and neck after long periods of sitting. No equipment is needed.

name: Open Book Rotation
description: Lie on your side with your knees bent and open your top arm across your body to rotate your chest. It relieves tension from desk work and improves posture. No equipment is needed.

name: Doorway Pec Stretch
description: Place your forearm on a door frame and step forward until you feel a stretch across your chest. It loosens the upper back and neck after long periods of sitting. It requires a door frame.

name: Bicep Curl
description: Curl a dumbbell up toward your shoulder and lower it slowly. It builds upper-body muscle and is meant for people who are already strong and pain free. It requires dumbbells.

name: Hammer Curl
description: Curl dumbbells with your palms facing each other and lower them slowly. It adds size and strength to the arms and chest and suits later stages of training. It requires dumbbells.

name: Lateral Raise
description: Lift dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height and lower them slowly. It builds upper-body muscle and is meant for people who are already strong and pain free. It requires dumbbells.

name: Front Raise
description: Lift dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height and lower them. It adds size and strength to the arms and chest and suits later stages of training. It requires dumbbells.

name: Arnold Press
description: Rotate dumbbells from palms facing you to palms facing forward as you press them overhead. It builds upper-body muscle and is meant for people who are already strong and pain free. It requires dumbbells.

name: Upright Row
description: Pull a barbell or dumbbells up along your body to chest height. It adds size and strength to the arms and chest and suits later stages of training. It requires a barbell or dumbbells.

name: Chest Fly
description: Lie on a bench, open your arms wide with dumbbells, then bring them back together. It builds upper-body muscle and is meant for people who are already strong and pain free. It requires dumbbells and a bench.

name: Bench Press
description: Lie on a bench and press a barbell up from your chest. It adds size and strength to the arms and chest and suits later stages of training. It requires a barbell and a bench.

name: Triceps Dip
description: Lower your body between two sturdy chairs by bending your elbows, then press back up. It builds upper-body muscle and is meant for people who are already strong and pain free. It requires two chairs or parallel bars.

name: Pull-Up
description: Hang from a bar and pull your chin above it, then lower slowly. It adds size and strength to the arms and chest and suits later stages of training. It requires a pull-up bar.

name: Superman Hold
description: Lie face down and lift your arms and legs a few inches, holding for five seconds. It builds trunk strength and is aimed at people who already move without back pain. No equipment is needed.

name: Side Plank
description: Support yourself on one forearm and the side of your foot, keeping your body in a straight line. It trains the muscles that brace the spine during heavy lifting and sport. No equipment is needed.

name: Pallof Press
description: Stand sideways to an anchored band and press your hands straight out without letting your torso twist. It builds trunk strength and is aimed at people who already move without back pain. It requires a resistance band.

name: Hollow Hold
description: Lie on your back and lift your shoulders and legs off the floor, holding the position. It trains the muscles that brace the spine during heavy lifting and sport. No equipment is needed.

name: Barbell Deadlift
description: Lift a loaded barbell from the floor to hip height with a flat back, then lower it with control. It builds trunk strength and is aimed at people who already move without back pain. It requires a barbell.

name: Back Extension on Bench
description: Lie face down over a back extension bench and raise your trunk until it is level with your legs. It trains the muscles that brace the spine during heavy lifting and sport. It requires a back extension bench.

name: Russian Twist
description: Sit leaning back with your feet raised and rotate your trunk from side to side. It builds trunk strength and is aimed at people who already move without back pain. No equipment is needed.

name: Mountain Climber
description: From a plank, drive your knees toward your chest in a quick alternating rhythm. It trains the muscles that brace the spine during heavy lifting and sport. No equipment is needed.

name: Box Jump
description: Jump onto a sturdy box with both feet and step back down. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. It requires a sturdy box.

name: Jump Rope
description: Swing a rope and hop over it with both feet. It raises the heart rate quickly and suits athletes and experienced exercisers. It requires a jump rope.

name: High Knees
description: Run in place, driving your knees up to hip height. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. No equipment is needed.

name: Tuck Jump
description: Jump straight up and pull your knees toward your chest before landing. It raises the heart rate quickly and suits athletes and experienced exercisers. No equipment is needed.

name: Skater Hop
description: Leap sideways from one foot to the other, landing softly on a bent knee. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. No equipment is needed.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: Swing a kettlebell from between your legs to chest height by snapping your hips forward. It raises the heart rate quickly and suits athletes and experienced exercisers. It requires a kettlebell.

name: Sprint Intervals
description: Sprint hard for 20 seconds, then walk for 60 seconds, and repeat. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. It requires open space or a treadmill.

name: Treadmill Jog
description: Jog at an easy pace on a treadmill for 15 to 30 minutes. It raises the heart rate quickly and suits athletes and experienced exercisers. It requires a treadmill.

name: Stair Climber
description: Step continuously on a stair climber machine at a steady pace. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. It requires a stair climber machine.

name: Battle Ropes
description: Whip heavy ropes up and down in alternating waves. It raises the heart rate quickly and suits athletes and experienced exercisers. It requires heavy ropes.

name: Depth Jump
description: Step off a low box, land, and immediately jump as high as you can. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. It requires a low box.

name: Hip Thrust with Barbell
description: Rest your upper back on a bench, roll a loaded barbell over your hips, and drive your hips up. It raises the heart rate quickly and suits athletes and experienced exercisers. It requires a barbell and a bench.

name: Cossack Squat
description: Take a wide stance and sink onto one bent leg while the other leg stays straight, then switch sides. It builds fitness and is high intensity, so it is usually left for later stages of training. No equipment is needed.

name: Downward Dog
description: From hands and knees, lift your hips up and back into an upside-down V. It combines flexibility and balance and is often taught in group classes. No equipment is needed.

name: Warrior II
description: Step your feet wide, bend your front knee, and extend your arms out to the sides. It links breathing with movement and is popular as a general fitness practice. No equipment is needed.

name: Tree Pose
description: Stand on one leg with the other foot resting on your inner calf or thigh and your hands together. It combines flexibility and balance and is often taught in group classes. No equipment is needed.

name: Eagle Pose
description: Wrap one leg and one arm around the other while balancing on a slightly bent leg. It links breathing with movement and is popular as a general fitness practice. No equipment is needed.

name: Boat Pose
description: Balance on your sit bones with your legs and chest lifted in a V shape. It combines flexibility and balance and is often taught in group classes. No equipment is needed.

name: Sun Salutation
description: Flow through a series of standing, folding, and plank poses in a smooth sequence. It links breathing with movement and is popular as a general fitness practice. No equipment is needed.
